drhp.business: Canara Robeco Asset Management Company Limited manages the Canara Robeco Mutual Fund, offering a suite of 27 open-ended mutual fund schemes spanning equity, debt, and hybrid categories. The Company serves a predominantly retail investor base of over 50.8 lakh folios through a pan-India network of 29 branches, 56,231 distributors, and a growing digital ecosystem. Its investment philosophy emphasizes bottom-up equity research focused on business quality and valuation, and fixed-income strategies prioritizing safety, liquidity, and returns.
drhp.end_markets: Indian retail and institutional investors across metropolitan centres, emerging cities, and B-30 (beyond top-30) cities|Offshore advisory clients
drhp.expansion: During FY 2025-26, the Company launched two new schemes: Canara Robeco Multi Asset Allocation Fund and Canara Robeco Banking and Financial Services Fund. As of March 31, 2026, the Canara Robeco Mutual Fund offered 27 schemes (10 debt-oriented, 13 equity-oriented, 4 hybrid). The Company also renamed Canara Robeco Consumer Trends Fund to Canara Robeco Consumption Fund, effective April 23, 2026, following SEBI no-objection and a unit-holder exit window. risks.note: Predominantly equity-oriented AUM (~90%) exposes revenue and portfolio valuations to equity and debt market fluctuations driven by macroeconomic factors, interest rates, and global developments.
Arises primarily in debt and hybrid portfolios during market stress or elevated redemptions; mitigated through active liquidity management, liquid instruments, and stress testing.
Damage to brand and investor trust from underperformance, mis-selling, operational lapses, or regulatory breaches could impair AUM and business viability.
Internal failuresâtrade execution errors, NAV calculation mistakes, settlement issues, system failures, or inadequate controlsâcan lead to financial loss and regulatory action.
SEBI regulations on expense ratios, product structures, and compliance requirements may impact operations and profitability; changes require continuous adaptation.
Exposure to unethical practices, inadequate risk awareness, or failure to adhere to internal policies could undermine the control environment and investor confidence.
Weak governance frameworks, lack of ownership, or insufficient oversight in decision-making processes may lead to strategic missteps and compliance failures.
